explanations.answer: Rebuild it like it was long ago
explanations.explanation: That's the promise, baker. The LORD says, "In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David. I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old…" (Amos 9:11). Gaps, ruins, all of it. I know what it's like to be a fallen thing, and this is the best news a fallen thing can hear.

explanations.answer: Leave it in ruins as a warning
explanations.explanation: Nope, no warning sign planted in the rubble here. The LORD says, "I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old…" (Amos 9:11). The ruins are getting fixed, not put on display. After all those heavy words earlier in the book, this one is a soft landing.

explanations.answer: Tear down what is left of it
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Look at the verbs the LORD picks: "restore," "repair," "rebuild" (Amos 9:11). Not one of them is "demolish." Whatever is left standing of that tent, He plans to build on it.

explanations.answer: Edom's remnant and the nations bearing His name
explanations.explanation: Yes! The LORD says it is "that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name…" (Amos 9:12). Edom's remnant is the part of Edom that is left. Then He adds the nations that bear His name, so the promise reaches past one neighbor.

explanations.answer: Philistia's cities and the whole land of Moab
explanations.explanation: Close neighbors, but not what the verse says. The LORD says they will possess "the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name" (Amos 9:12). Philistia and Moab don't show up in that line at all. Edom is the name to hold onto.

explanations.answer: Egypt's fields and the faraway land of Cush
explanations.explanation: That's a long trip for a promise that doesn't go there. The verse says "the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name" (Amos 9:12). No Egypt, no Cush. I'd pack a lighter bag, friend, because the answer is right next door in Edom.

explanations.answer: Plowing starting before the reaping is done
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. "…the plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes, the sower of seed" (Amos 9:13). The plowman is already showing up while the reaper is still out working. It's like the harvest is so big the next job can't wait its turn.

explanations.answer: Fields lying unplowed for many years
explanations.explanation: Flip that one over, friend. A plowman overtaking the reaper means plowing is catching up fast, not sitting around (Amos 9:13). Nothing in the verse has a field waiting years for anybody. Everybody is busy and everybody is on time.

explanations.answer: Reapers leaving the grain in the field
explanations.explanation: Good guess if you were picturing a slow harvest, but the verse goes the other way. "…the plowman will overtake the reaper…" (Amos 9:13). The reaper isn't leaving anything behind. The reaper is working, and the plowman is right on his heels.

Right on, baker. "I will restore My people Israel from captivity; they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities" (Amos 9:14). They don't just fix the buildings and wave at them from the road. They move in and live there.

Rebuild a city and then walk away from it? That would be a lot of work for nothing. The verse says they "will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities" (Amos 9:14). Inhabit means they live in the cities they rebuilt.

I get it, selling is what people do with fixed-up places. But that's not in the verse. The LORD says, "they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities" (Amos 9:14). These folks are building homes to live in, not to flip.

True, and listen to the verse: "They will plant vineyards and drink their wine…" (Amos 9:14). Planting and drinking go together here. That's a big turn from the earlier warning in Amos 5:11, where the vineyards were planted but the wine wasn't theirs to drink.

It's actually True, friend. The LORD says, "They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit" (Amos 9:14). Same people planting, same people drinking. Compare that with Amos 5:11, where the wine of their vineyards wasn't going to be theirs.

explanations.answer: They will never again be uprooted
explanations.explanation: That's the promise, baker. "I will firmly plant them in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). Firmly planted, like a tree with roots that go all the way down. And the LORD is the one doing the planting.

explanations.answer: They will be uprooted once more
explanations.explanation: Nope, the verse closes that door. The LORD says they will be planted "never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). "Never again" doesn't leave room for one more round.

explanations.answer: They will move on to a new land
explanations.explanation: No moving trucks in this verse, friend. The LORD says He will firmly plant them "in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). They stay planted in the land He gave them.
Flip it around, baker. The LORD calls it "the land that I have given them" (Amos 9:15). A given land is a gift, not a prize somebody won. Nobody wins a gift, you just get to say thank you.
Right, it's False. The verse says "…never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them…" (Amos 9:15). The LORD is the one who gave it. It's a gift, not something they won for themselves.
